# An exploration of the Lorenz Attractor and Makie Animation

The lorenz attractor is a beautiful example of chaotic systems.
These are traditionally defined as systems that are deterministic but very small differences
in initial conditions lead to vastly different, seemingly unpredictable, outcomes.
They are defined by the following differential equations:

\begin{align}
\frac{dx}{dt} &= \sigma (y - x) \\
\frac{dy}{dt} &= x (\rho - z) - y \\
\frac{dz}{dt} &= x y - \beta z
\end{align}


```{julia}
Base.@kwdef mutable struct Lorenz
    # parameters
    dt::Float64 = 0.01
    σ::Float64 = 10
    ρ::Float64 = 28
    β::Float64 = 8/3
    # Initial conditions
    x::Float64 = 1
    y::Float64 = 1
    z::Float64 = 1
end
```

```{julia}
function step!(l::Lorenz)
    # Differential Equations
    dx = l.σ * (l.y - l.x)
    dy = l.x * (l.ρ- l.z) - l.y
    dz = l.x * l.y - l.β * l.z
    # Euler Step
    l.x += l.dt * dx
    l.y += l.dt * dy
    l.z += l.dt * dz
    # Return 3D point
    Point3f(l.x, l.y, l.z)
end
```

```{julia}
dark_latexfonts = merge(theme_dark(), theme_latexfonts());
```

```{julia}
function plot_lorenz(; fname="lorenz.mp4", hist_length=200, N_frames=1000, colormap=:viridis)
    attractor = Lorenz()
    points = Observable(CircularBuffer{Point3f}(hist_length))
    colors = Observable(Int[])

    fig = Figure()
    ax = Axis3(
        fig[1,1],
        protrusions=(0, 0, 0, 0),
        viewmode=:fit,
        limits=(-30, 30, -30, 30, 0, 50)
    )
    l = lines!(ax, points, color=colors, colormap=colormap, transparency=true)

    record(fig, fname, 1:N_frames, framerate=30) do frame
        push!(points[], step!(attractor))
        push!(colors[], min(length(points[]), 100))
        l.colorrange = (0, min(length(points[]), 100))
        colors[] = colors[]
        points[] = points[]
        ax.azimuth[] = 1.7pi + 0.3 * sin(2pi * frame / N_frames)
    end
end
```

```{julia}
with_theme(dark_latexfonts) do
    plot_lorenz()
end
```

## Interactive GLMakie Plot

The following code can be used to make the lorenz plot interactive.
It adds a run button which pauses/plays the simulation.
It also includes a menu to change the colormap used to show the history of the simulation.

```{julia}
#| eval: false

menu = Menu(fig, options=["viridis", "inferno", "magma", "plasma"])

on(menu.selection) do cmap 
    l.colormap = cmap
end
notify(menu.selection)

run = Button(fig[2, 1]; label="run", tellwidth=false)
isrunning = Observable(false)
on(run.clicks) do clicks; isrunning[] = !isrunning[]; end
on(run.clicks) do clicks
    @async while isrunning[]
        isopen(fig.scene) || break
        push!(points[], step!(attractor))
        push!(colors[], min(length(points[]), 100))
        l.colorrange = (0, min(length(points[]), 100))
        colors[] = colors[]
        points[] = points[]
        sleep(0.001)
    end
end 
```

## Multiple Lorenz Simulations

Of course the main thing people discuss with Lorenz systems is that it is an example of a chaotic system.
The general definition for chatoic systems are:
> Systems where minute changes in initial conditions lead to vastly different outcomes.
To visualize how the chaotic nature of the system the following visualization includes multiple starting conditions to see how the outcomes differ.

Helper function to fade the colormap
```{julia}
function fade_colormap(color::Colorant, n=256)
    r, g, b = red(color), green(color), blue(color)
    colors = [RGBA(r, g, b, α^5) for α in LinRange(0f0, 1f0, n)]
    return ColorScheme(colors)
end
```

```{julia}
function multi_lorenz(; fname="multi_lorenz.mp4", npoints=300, N_frames=1000, framerate=30)
    eps = 1e-8
    num = 10
    attractors = [
        Lorenz(z=1+(n-1)*eps)
        for n in 1:num
            ]

    all_points = [
        Observable(CircularBuffer{Point3f}(npoints))
        for n in 1:num
            ]
    all_colors = [
        Observable(Float32[])
        for n in 1:num
            ]

    blues = [get(ColorSchemes.Blues, t) for t in LinRange(0.5, 0.8, num)]
    cmaps = [fade_colormap(c) for c in blues]

    fig = Figure(size=(10inch, 7inch), fontsize=18pt)
    ax = Axis3(fig[1,2],
               protrusions=(0, 60, 0, 0),
               viewmode=:fit,
               limits = (-30,30,-30,30,0,50),
               )
    Label(fig[1, :, Top()], "Lorenz Attractor",
          fontsize=30pt,
          color=:white,
          valign=:bottom,
          )
    for (i, points) in enumerate(all_points)
        lines!(ax, points; color=all_colors[i], colormap=cmaps[i], transparency=true)
    end

    eq_layout = fig[1,1] = GridLayout(tellwidth=false, tellheight=false)

    Label(eq_layout[1, 1],
          L"\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = \sigma(y - x)",
          fontsize=30pt, color=:white, halign=:left) 
    Label(eq_layout[2, 1],
          L"\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = x(\rho - z) - y",
          fontsize=30pt, color=:white, halign=:left)
    Label(eq_layout[3, 1],
          L"\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}t} = xy - \beta z",
          fontsize=30pt, color=:white, halign=:left)

    record(fig, fname, 1:N_frames, framerate=framerate) do frame
        for (attractor, points, colors) in zip(attractors, all_points, all_colors)
            push!(points[], step!(attractor))
            n = length(points[])
            colors[] = n <= 1 ? Float32[1f0] : collect(LinRange(0f0, 1f0, n))
            points[] = points[]
        end
        ax.azimuth[] = 1.7pi + 0.3 * sin(2pi * frame / (0.5 * N_frames))
    end
end
```

```{julia}
with_theme(dark_latexfonts) do
    multi_lorenz(; N_frames=Int(3e3), framerate=60)
end
```

Interactive version:
```{julia}
#| eval: false
function reset!()
    for i in 1:num 
        empty!(all_points[i][])
        all_points[i][] = all_points[i][]
        all_colors[i][] = Float32[]
        attractors[i] = Lorenz(z=1+(i-1)*eps)
    end
end


button_layout = fig[2, 1:2] = GridLayout()
run = Button(button_layout[2, 1]; label="run")
reset = Button(button_layout[2, 2]; label="reset")

rowsize!(fig.layout, 2, Fixed(40))

on(reset.clicks) do _ 
    isrunning[] = false 
    sleep(0.05) 
    reset!()
end


isrunning = Observable(false)
on(run.clicks) do clicks; isrunning[] = !isrunning[]; end
on(run.clicks) do clicks
    @async while isrunning[]
        isopen(fig.scene) || break 
        for (attractor, points, colors) in zip(attractors, all_points, all_colors)
            push!(points[], step!(attractor))
            n = length(points[])
            colors[] = n <= 1 ? Float32[1f0] : collect(LinRange(0f0, 1f0, n))
            points[] = points[]
        end
        sleep(8e-3)
    end
end
```
